summary: This paper delivers three rigorous quantitative and analytic advances on Shunia's deterministic polynomial-time equivalence between abundance decisions and integer factorization (arXiv:2611.34242v1). First, an elementary telescoping odd-square tail bound cuts Shunia's Lemma 3.2 exponent by 16x to J >= max(2, ceil(log2 w)) with sharpness within 2 on w = 2p, while rescaling the Hankel system to mu_i = B/q_i in [1, 3) achieves exact Vandermonde denominator cancellation to collapse the perturbation factor from n^12 to n^4 and shrink Theorem 3.1's exponent by 19x (361x smaller abundance query bit-length). Second, for omega(n) <= k, the exponent drops from quadratic to linear O(k log n) with 2k nonadaptive sums (4 sums for k = 2), and Baker-Harman-Pintz tightening compresses Algorithm 1's sieve from O((log x)^16) to O((log x)^(17/2)). Third, at Shunia's open endpoint c = 1, smooth prime density yields a strict deficit, whereas under any quasi-RH (Theta < 1), Diamond-Pintz oscillation (Theta = 1/2) and a Landau-Mellin argument (Theta in (1/2, 1)) yield infinitely many squarefree abundant integers with P^-(z) > sqrt(log z).
strengths: Sharp, elementary 16x improvement to Shunia's Lemma 3.2 threshold via the odd-square telescoping bound, paired with an explicit w = 2p sharpness witness within additive gap 2.

Clever analytic preconditioning of the Hankel system via mu_i = B/q_i in [1, 3) that cancels B^(l-2) in the Vandermonde denominator, reducing the perturbation factor from n^12 to n^4 with proved universal bounds K_3(l) < 2^53 and yielding a 19x exponent contraction (361x query bit-length reduction) without altering the runtime algorithm.

Quadratic-to-linear exponent collapse J = O(k log n) for bounded omega(n) <= k (including an unconditional 4-sample, J = 4M + 10 algorithm for k = 2 even for twin primes) and a 7.5-degree sieve compression to O((log x)^(17/2)) via Baker-Harman-Pintz exponent optimization.

Complete resolution of the c = 1 endpoint under any quasi-Riemann Hypothesis (Theta < 1), cleanly contrasting the exact smooth-prime deficit against Diamond-Pintz oscillations at Theta = 1/2 and a rigorous Landau-Mellin branch-point proof for Theta in (1/2, 1) that overcomes both Chebyshev bias and upper-cutoff errors.
weaknesses: The existence of infinitely many abundant integers at the critical boundary c = 1 (Theorem 3(b)) remains conditional on Theta < 1 (quasi-RH); the unconditional case Theta = 1 stays open.

Theorem 3(a) characterizes an idealized smooth-prime model (theta(t) = t) rather than actual primes, and the logarithmic integral convention li(t) = int_2^t dv/log v (zero below 2) in Section 4's Laplace transform could be stated explicitly.

While 20 constructive Lean 4.35.0 lemmas and SHA-256 verification scripts are cited, this manuscript-only assessment did not independently execute the external repository artifacts, and the analytic number theory arguments in Theorem 3 remain hand-proved rather than formalized.
